name: Wheat flour
function: Provides structure, texture and bulk in baked and processed foods.
common_uses: Bread, pasta, crackers, breading/coatings, thickeners in sauces.
allergen_info: Contains gluten. Direct allergen: wheat. Also relevant to people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.
health_considerations: A source of carbohydrates and some protein. Refined wheat flour has less fiber than whole wheat flour.
source: Codex Alimentarius / FDA Food Labeling Guide (general food composition references)

name: Sugar
function: Sweetens food and can act as a preservative and texture/browning agent.
common_uses: Virtually all sweetened processed foods, baked goods, beverages, sauces.
allergen_info: Not a recognized allergen.
health_considerations: The retrieved information notes that health guidelines commonly recommend limiting added sugar intake as part of a balanced diet.
source: WHO guideline on sugars intake (general public guidance)

name: Palm oil
function: Provides texture, mouthfeel, and shelf stability; used as a cooking/frying fat.
common_uses: Margarine, packaged snacks, baked goods, instant noodles.
allergen_info: Not a recognized common allergen.
health_considerations: The retrieved information notes palm oil is high in saturated fat compared to many other vegetable oils; general dietary guidance suggests moderating saturated fat intake.
source: FAO/WHO food composition references (general public guidance)

name: Milk solids
function: Adds body, creaminess, and protein/nutritional content.
common_uses: Chocolate, baked goods, processed cheese, instant products.
allergen_info: Contains milk. Direct allergen: milk. Relevant for lactose intolerance and milk protein allergy.
health_considerations: A source of protein and calcium; also contributes lactose and dairy fat.
source: FDA Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act (FALCPA) reference list

name: Soy
function: Provides protein, texture, and can act as a filler or meat extender.
common_uses: Processed meats, meat substitutes, sauces, baked goods.
allergen_info: Direct allergen: soy. One of the major recognized food allergens.
health_considerations: A plant-based protein source; minimally processed soy also provides fiber and micronutrients.
source: FDA major food allergen list

name: Whey
function: Adds protein and can improve texture/moisture retention.
common_uses: Protein bars/powders, baked goods, processed cheese, infant formula.
allergen_info: Derived from milk. Contains milk allergen.
health_considerations: A high-quality protein source derived from milk processing (cheese-making byproduct).
source: FDA Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act (FALCPA) reference list

name: Casein
function: Provides protein structure, emulsification, and creaminess.
common_uses: Processed cheese, coffee creamers, protein supplements.
allergen_info: Derived from milk. Contains milk allergen.
health_considerations: The primary protein found in milk; a concentrated dairy protein source.
source: FDA Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act (FALCPA) reference list

name: E100 - Curcumin
function: Natural yellow-orange food coloring derived from turmeric.
common_uses: Mustards, cheeses, snack foods, baked goods.
allergen_info: Not a recognized common allergen; derived from turmeric (spice).
health_considerations: Approved food colorant in most jurisdictions within regulated limits.
source: EU Food Additives Database / Codex Alimentarius

name: E202 - Potassium sorbate
function: Inhibits mold and yeast growth, extending shelf life.
common_uses: Cheese, baked goods, wine, dried fruits, beverages.
allergen_info: Not a recognized common allergen.
health_considerations: Widely used preservative considered safe within regulated levels by major food safety authorities.
source: EU Food Additives Database / Codex Alimentarius

name: E211 - Sodium benzoate
function: Antimicrobial preservative, inhibits bacteria, yeast and mold.
common_uses: Carbonated drinks, fruit juices, pickles, sauces.
allergen_info: Not a recognized common allergen.
health_considerations: The retrieved information notes some regulatory bodies have studied its interaction with ascorbic acid (vitamin C), which can form trace benzene; approved within regulated limits.
source: EU Food Additives Database / EFSA opinions

name: E220 - Sulfur dioxide
function: Antioxidant and preservative; prevents browning and microbial spoilage.
common_uses: Dried fruits, wine, processed potatoes.
allergen_info: Can trigger sensitivity reactions in sulfite-sensitive individuals, particularly those with asthma; commonly required to be labeled.
health_considerations: Regulatory bodies require labeling due to known sensitivity reactions in a subset of the population.
source: EU Food Additives Database / FDA sulfite labeling requirements

name: E300 - Ascorbic acid (Vitamin C)
function: Antioxidant that prevents oxidation/browning; also a nutrient (Vitamin C).
common_uses: Juices, cured meats, baked goods, fruit preparations.
allergen_info: Not a recognized common allergen.
health_considerations: Also an essential vitamin; used both for nutritional fortification and as a processing aid.
source: EU Food Additives Database / Codex Alimentarius

name: E322 - Lecithin
function: Emulsifier; helps blend ingredients that would otherwise separate (e.g. fat and water).
common_uses: Chocolate, margarine, baked goods, instant products.
allergen_info: When derived from soy, may be relevant to soy allergy; sunflower-derived lecithin is not a soy allergen.
health_considerations: Generally recognized as safe by major food safety authorities within typical usage levels.
source: EU Food Additives Database / Codex Alimentarius

name: E330 - Citric acid
function: Acidity regulator and preservative; adds tartness and helps preserve freshness.
common_uses: Soft drinks, candies, canned foods, sauces.
allergen_info: Not a recognized common allergen.
health_considerations: One of the most widely used food acids; considered safe within regulated levels.
source: EU Food Additives Database / Codex Alimentarius

name: E407 - Carrageenan
function: Thickening and gelling agent derived from red seaweed.
common_uses: Dairy products, plant-based milks, processed meats, desserts.
allergen_info: Not a recognized common allergen.
health_considerations: The retrieved information notes ongoing scientific discussion regarding degraded carrageenan and digestive effects; food-grade carrageenan is regulated separately and approved within set limits.
source: EU Food Additives Database / Codex Alimentarius

name: E412 - Guar gum
function: Thickening agent derived from guar beans; improves texture and viscosity.
common_uses: Sauces, dairy products, gluten-free baked goods, ice cream.
allergen_info: Not a recognized common allergen; derived from legumes (guar bean), a distinct plant family from peanuts.
health_considerations: A soluble dietary fiber; generally recognized as safe within regulated levels.
source: EU Food Additives Database / Codex Alimentarius

name: E415 - Xanthan gum
function: Thickening and stabilizing agent produced by bacterial fermentation of sugars.
common_uses: Salad dressings, gluten-free products, sauces.
allergen_info: Not a recognized common allergen; may be produced using corn, soy, or wheat-based sugars in fermentation, though the final purified additive is not typically considered allergenic.
health_considerations: Widely used and considered safe within regulated levels by major food safety authorities.
source: EU Food Additives Database / Codex Alimentarius

name: E420 - Sorbitol
function: Sugar alcohol used as a low-calorie sweetener and moisture-retaining agent.
common_uses: Sugar-free gum, diet foods, candies.
allergen_info: Not a recognized common allergen.
health_considerations: The retrieved information notes sugar alcohols can have a laxative effect in some individuals when consumed in large amounts.
source: EU Food Additives Database / Codex Alimentarius

name: E621 - Monosodium glutamate (MSG)
function: Flavor enhancer that intensifies savory (umami) taste.
common_uses: Instant noodles, snack foods, seasonings, processed soups.
allergen_info: Not classified as a major allergen; some individuals report sensitivity/reactions, a topic which has been studied by food safety authorities.
health_considerations: Major food safety authorities, including the FDA and EFSA, generally recognize MSG as safe within typical dietary levels.
source: FDA MSG information page / EFSA opinions

name: Milk (allergen group)
function: Allergen reference entry, not an ingredient function.
common_uses: N/A
allergen_info: Milk is one of the major recognized food allergens. Common label synonyms include milk powder, milk solids, whey, casein/caseinate, and lactose (lactose itself is a sugar, not the allergenic protein, but often indicates dairy origin).
health_considerations: Relevant for individuals with milk allergy or lactose intolerance (two distinct conditions).
source: FDA major food allergen list (FALCPA)

name: Wheat/Gluten (allergen group)
function: Allergen reference entry, not an ingredient function.
common_uses: N/A
allergen_info: Wheat is a major recognized food allergen. Gluten (found in wheat, barley, rye) is separately relevant to individuals with celiac disease or non-celiac gluten sensitivity.
health_considerations: Relevant for wheat allergy and celiac disease/gluten sensitivity (distinct conditions).
source: FDA major food allergen list (FALCPA)

name: Soy (allergen group)
function: Allergen reference entry, not an ingredient function.
common_uses: N/A
allergen_info: Soy is one of the major recognized food allergens. Soy lecithin (E322) is a highly refined derivative that some allergy guidance treats as lower-risk, though sensitive individuals are still advised to check with a professional.
health_considerations: Relevant for individuals with soy allergy.
source: FDA major food allergen list (FALCPA)

name: Peanuts (allergen group)
function: Allergen reference entry, not an ingredient function.
common_uses: N/A
allergen_info: Peanuts are one of the major recognized food allergens and a common cause of severe allergic reactions.
health_considerations: Relevant for individuals with peanut allergy.
source: FDA major food allergen list (FALCPA)

name: Tree nuts (allergen group)
function: Allergen reference entry, not an ingredient function.
common_uses: N/A
allergen_info: Tree nuts are among the major recognized food allergens; distinct from peanuts (which are a legume).
health_considerations: Relevant for individuals with tree nut allergy.
source: FDA major food allergen list (FALCPA)

name: Eggs (allergen group)
function: Allergen reference entry, not an ingredient function.
common_uses: N/A
allergen_info: Eggs are one of the major recognized food allergens.
health_considerations: Relevant for individuals with egg allergy.
source: FDA major food allergen list (FALCPA)

name: Fish and Shellfish (allergen groups)
function: Allergen reference entry, not an ingredient function.
common_uses: N/A
allergen_info: Fish and shellfish (crustacean shellfish) are separately recognized major allergens.
health_considerations: Relevant for individuals with fish or shellfish allergy.
source: FDA major food allergen list (FALCPA)

name: Sesame (allergen group)
function: Allergen reference entry, not an ingredient function.
common_uses: N/A
allergen_info: Sesame was added as a major recognized food allergen in several jurisdictions in recent years (e.g. FASTER Act in the US, effective 2023).
health_considerations: Relevant for individuals with sesame allergy.
source: FDA FASTER Act allergen labeling update

name: Potato
function: Primary whole-food base ingredient providing structure, carbohydrates, and texture in crisps and snacks.
common_uses: Potato chips, crisps, extruded snacks, french fries, dehydrated flakes.
allergen_info: Not a recognized common allergen.
health_considerations: Naturally gluten-free whole food ingredient; deep-frying in oil adds dietary fat and calories.
source: USDA FoodData Central / Codex Alimentarius food composition guide

name: Rice bran oil
function: High-stability cooking and frying oil with a high smoke point and neutral flavor.
common_uses: Deep-fried snack foods, crisps, stir-frying, blended edible vegetable oils.
allergen_info: Not a recognized common allergen.
health_considerations: Contains heart-healthy monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats along with natural antioxidant gamma-oryzanol.
source: Codex Standard for Named Vegetable Oils (CODEX STAN 210-1999)

name: Palmolein
function: Liquid fraction of palm oil widely used for frying snacks due to exceptional oxidation resistance and crisp texture retention.
common_uses: Potato chips, namkeens, instant noodles, commercial frying.
allergen_info: Not a recognized common allergen.
health_considerations: Contains a blend of saturated and unsaturated fatty acids; moderating total dietary saturated fat intake is advised by WHO.
source: Codex Standard for Named Vegetable Oils (CODEX STAN 210-1999)

name: Iodized salt / Black salt
function: Essential culinary seasoning enhancing savory taste; iodized to prevent iodine deficiency; black salt adds characteristic sulfurous mineral flavor.
common_uses: Snack seasonings, spice blends, chips, chaat masala, table salt.
allergen_info: Not a recognized food allergen.
health_considerations: Provides essential sodium and trace minerals; health authorities advise moderating daily sodium intake to support cardiovascular health.
source: WHO Guideline: Sodium intake for adults and children

name: Maltodextrin
function: Easily digestible carbohydrate powder used as a flavor carrier, dispersant, and texture stabilizer in seasoning blends.
common_uses: Dry spice mixes, snack seasonings, powdered beverages, sports nutrition.
allergen_info: Usually produced from corn, rice, or potato starch. When produced from wheat, extensive hydrolysis removes gluten proteins; recognized as safe for celiac diets in standard refined forms.
health_considerations: High glycemic index carbohydrate; acts metabolically similar to simple sugars.
source: FDA 21 CFR 184.1444 / EFSA Panel on Dietetic Products

name: Tomato powder
function: Provides natural tangy tomato flavor, umami depth, and natural red coloring.
common_uses: Tomato-flavored chips, pasta sauces, snack seasonings, soup bases.
allergen_info: Not a recognized major allergen. Nightshade family fruit derivative.
health_considerations: Natural source of lycopene and dietary organic acids.
source: USDA FoodData Central / Codex Food Composition

name: Onion and Garlic powder
function: Aromatic allium vegetable seasonings imparting savory, pungent, and umami taste profiles.
common_uses: Potato chips, snack seasonings, spice blends, processed culinary foods.
allergen_info: Not classified as a major food allergen under FALCPA; some individuals have allium intolerances (FODMAP sensitivities).
health_considerations: Natural vegetable powders containing natural organosulfur compounds.
source: Codex Alimentarius / FDA Spice Guidelines

name: Spices and Condiments
function: Complex proprietary blend of culinary spices (e.g. cumin, coriander, red chili, black pepper, clove, fenugreek) providing aroma and heat.
common_uses: Masala chips, extruded snacks, savory crisps, curries.
allergen_info: Generally non-allergenic; mustard and celery when present in spice blends require distinct labeling in certain international jurisdictions.
health_considerations: Natural botanical aromatic spices with natural antioxidant polyphenols.
source: Codex STAN 192-1995 / International Spices Standard

name: E296 - Malic acid
function: Natural organic fruit acid providing a smooth, tart, and lingering sour flavor that enhances fruit and spice notes.
common_uses: Potato chips, sour candies, carbonated beverages, fruit snacks, seasonings.
allergen_info: Not a recognized food allergen.
health_considerations: Naturally occurring metabolic acid found in apples; generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA and JECFA.
source: Codex Alimentarius INS 296 / FDA 21 CFR 184.1069

name: E334 - Tartaric acid
category: food additive - acidity regulator / antioxidant synergist
function: Organic acid providing a sharp, crisp sour taste and acting as an antioxidant synergist.
common_uses: Snack food seasonings, baked goods, wine, grape-flavored products, confectionery.
allergen_info: Not a recognized food allergen.
health_considerations: Naturally present in grapes and tamarind; safe within regulated food standards.
source: Codex Alimentarius INS 334 / EFSA Food Additives Opinion

name: E551 - Silicon dioxide
function: Inert food-grade mineral powder that absorbs ambient moisture to maintain free-flowing properties in powdered seasonings.
common_uses: Snack seasoning dusts, spice mixes, powdered drink mixes, table salt.
allergen_info: Not a recognized food allergen. Inorganic mineral compound.
health_considerations: Inert mineral approved globally by FDA, EFSA, and Codex Alimentarius with established safe acceptable intake levels.
source: Codex Alimentarius INS 551 / FDA 21 CFR 172.480

name: E160c - Paprika extract (Capsanthin / Capsorubin)
function: Natural oil-soluble red-orange carotenoid pigment extracted from sweet red bell peppers (Capsicum annuum).
common_uses: Potato chips, snack seasonings, processed cheese, sausages, sauces.
allergen_info: Not a major food allergen. Derived from sweet red peppers.
health_considerations: Natural carotenoid antioxidant pigment; safe and widely approved worldwide.
source: Codex Alimentarius INS 160c / JECFA Specifications

name: Flavouring substances (Natural & Nature-Identical)
function: Food-grade aroma molecules and botanical extracts that provide consistent, appealing taste profiles to processed foods.
common_uses: Savory crisps, snacks, beverages, confectionery.
allergen_info: Regulations require explicit labeling if flavoring substances originate from major allergens (e.g. celery, mustard, dairy).
health_considerations: Evaluated and approved by JECFA (Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives) and FEMA (Flavor and Extract Manufacturers Association).
source: Codex Guidelines for the Use of Flavourings (CAC/GL 66-2008)

name: E440 - Pectin
function: Natural plant-derived soluble dietary fiber from citrus peels and apples used as a gelling agent and stabilizer.
common_uses: Fruit crushes, jams, fruit beverages, yogurts, confectionery.
allergen_info: Not a recognized common allergen.
health_considerations: Natural soluble dietary fiber supporting digestive wellness; recognized as safe worldwide.
source: Codex Alimentarius INS 440 / JECFA Specifications

name: E466 - Sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC)
function: Cellulose derivative providing uniform mouthfeel, suspension of fruit particles, and emulsion stability.
common_uses: Flavored milk drinks, ice creams, fruit syrups, salad dressings.
allergen_info: Not a recognized food allergen.
health_considerations: Indigestible dietary polymer acting as dietary fiber; approved safe by FDA and EFSA.
source: Codex Alimentarius INS 466 / FDA 21 CFR 182.1745

name: E127 - Erythrosine
function: Organoiodine dye providing bright pink/cherry-red hue to fruit-flavored drinks and confectionery.
common_uses: Maraschino cherries, strawberry milk drinks, cake decorations.
allergen_info: Not a protein allergen; regulated with strict acceptable daily intake (ADI) limits.
health_considerations: Studied by regulatory agencies regarding thyroid hormone metabolism at high dosages; approved within strict regulated maximum levels.
source: EFSA Scientific Opinion on Erythrosine / Codex STAN 192-1995

name: Fruit Crush / Strawberry Pulp
function: Provides authentic fruit taste, natural acidity, natural antioxidants (vitamin C), and fruit fiber.
common_uses: Flavored milkshakes, ice creams, fruit yogurts, bakery toppings.
allergen_info: Not classified as a major food allergen under FALCPA/Codex.
health_considerations: Natural source of anthocyanin antioxidants and micronutrients.
source: USDA FoodData Central / Codex Fruit Guidelines
